title: Tiled GEMM: data reuse and arithmetic intensity

steps.title: Naive GEMM: one thread per output
Transposed staging and vectorized memory access

cases.name: tiny
cases.purpose: Smaller than any tile, small integer inputs, exact results (tolerance 0): checks indices, bounds checks, and that accumulation starts from 0.

cases.name: one_tile
cases.purpose: Exactly one 128×128 block tile and 4 slices of BK=8: with tail issues ruled out, checks micro-tile coordinates and the K loop.

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: M, N and K are not multiples of the tile, and K is not a multiple of 4: checks tail zero-filling and the scalar fallback path of float4.

cases.name: tail_vec
cases.purpose: K and N are multiples of 4 but M and N are not multiples of 128: tail tiles on the float4 path.

cases.name: k1
cases.purpose: K = 1: only one incomplete K slice; C is an outer product.

cases.name: row
cases.purpose: M = 1 (matrix-vector product): the grid has only one row of blocks, and most threads are out of bounds.

cases.name: col
cases.purpose: N = 1: tells the roles of A and B apart; B has only one row.

cases.name: long_k
cases.purpose: Long reduction: the K loop runs 512 slices, and the tolerance grows with sqrt(K).

cases.name: square
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data, every element checked.

cases.name: square4k
cases.purpose: 137 GFLOP, arithmetic intensity about 683 FLOP/B: far to the right of the ridge point; measures FP32 compute throughput.

cases.name: wide
cases.purpose: C is 256 MB, larger than L2; K is shorter, so writing back C is a larger share of the work.
